David / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As I mentioned, Clearline had a partial service disruption in April that affected two of our regional ingestion pipelines. Our engineering team traced it to model-serving latency spikes during a peak window; it impacted several downstream patient-facing reports for ~6 hours. We appreciate Redwood’s investigation and the post-mortem so far.

We are approaching our renewal window (contract expires 2029-05-31) and leadership has asked me to request a retention package to keep us on platform. Specifically we need:
- A one-time credit for operational impact (we are requesting USD 35,000)
- A 12-month term reset (move to a fresh 12-month term starting 2029-06-01)
- An SLA addendum guaranteeing 99.9% availability for critical ingestion pipelines, with a 3-month observability trial at no extra cost

We are prepared to sign within two weeks if we can get a commercial anchor (credit + SLA addendum). We prefer to keep things simple — happy to do a 12-month renewal if that’s what you need.

I’ve attached our outage report and a short list of affected endpoints. Please let me know what Redwood can do.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Data Platform, Clearline Health

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the note and the outage packet — sorry again for the disruption. We want Clearline to stay on a dependable plan and to rebuild trust quickly. I put together a practical retention offer we can commit to immediately while we finalize legal language:

Proposed bridge offer (pre-approval):
- One-time operational credit: USD 25,000 applied to the first invoice after renewal
- Term: 12-month reset starting 2029-06-01
- SLA addendum: 3-month complimentary SLA observability + 99.9% uptime target for listed ingestion endpoints; if we miss the target we will provide additional pro-rated credits per existing SLA table
- Optional: if you convert to a 24-month commitment at signing, we can increase the one-time credit to USD 35,000 and add a proactive runbook review from our reliability team

Quick notes: the 25k credit and the 3-month SLA addendum are within my deal desk authority; increasing to 35k or offering beyond the SLA language (longer credits or deeper price concession) needs exec sign-off and finance alignment.

Marissa / Vivek — can you confirm economics and whether finance will accept the 25k + 3-month SLA trail as the baseline? If Clearline counters to insist on 35k, they are escalating to procurement and I expect they will ask for an additional 10% off list for year-one. I’ve included the outage report and an initial econ model.

Alyssa — if that baseline looks acceptable, I’ll get legal to prepare the addendum and we can circulate a one-page MOU to speed signature.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
